content:
EXECUTIVES. DATA LEADERS. TRANSFORMATION LEADERS.

 I’ve been thinking about DOLLY PARTON today.

 Her music was part of the soundtrack of my childhood. 
 My parents listened to Dolly, so I grew up hearing her voice, 
 her stories, her humor, and her songs.

 But as I’ve gotten older, I realize it wasn’t just the music that stayed with me.

 It was how UNAPOLOGETICALLY she showed up as herself.

 Big personality.
 Big ambition.
 Big hair.
 Big voice.

 And somehow, none of it came at the expense of HUMILITY, KINDNESS, or HARD WORK.
 That combination has always fascinated me.

 Because in EXECUTIVE LEADERSHIP, DATA, TECHNOLOGY, and TRANSFORMATION, 
 there can be tremendous pressure to fit a certain mold.

 Be polished.
 Be strategic.
 Be measured.
 Be “executive.”

 Sometimes we're subtly taught that leadership means becoming a little less of ourselves.

 Dolly reminds me of the opposite.

 You can be BOLD without being arrogant.
 You can be AMBITIOUS without losing your humanity.
 You can have a big personality and still make room for other people.

 And you don't have to apologize for taking up space.

 That lesson means more to me now than it did when I was younger.

 Because leadership isn't about shrinking yourself so other people feel comfortable.

 It's about knowing who you are.
 Knowing what you stand for.
 And having the courage to bring that person into the room.

 The older I get, the less interested I am in being the most impressive person in the room.

 I'm much more interested in being the person who MAKES THE ROOM BETTER.

 The person who develops people.
 Shares what she knows.
 Creates opportunities.
 Opens doors.
 And leaves something behind that matters.

 That's the kind of leadership I want.

 Maybe that's why Dolly has stayed with me all these years.

 I first knew her through my parents' music. 
 I grew up admiring her confidence and individuality.

 And today, I appreciate something even deeper:
 She never seemed to lose herself while becoming successful.
 That's a lesson worth carrying into ANY CAREER. 💛

 Who was someone you grew up hearing, watching, or admiring who quietly shaped the leader you became?

 EXECUTIVES. DATA LEADERS. TRANSFORMATION LEADERS: 
 Leadership Shouldn’t Cost You WHO YOU ARE. Don’t Shrink Yourself to Fit the Room.

comment: A key leadership test is whether authenticity scales. The best leaders don't just bring their personality into the room—they create an environment where others feel safe bringing theirs too.
